A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, models, and principal experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation analyses, primitive-vector interventions, composition and transfer experiments, and nearest-neighbor strategy analyses, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds automated annotation results, intervention controls, interference analyses, and clustering robustness experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o cluster annotation, algorithmic-versus-linguistic grouping, and expressivity-based ranking to the manually interpreted pipeline in v1 (Section 4.2; Appendices A.7 and C). This substantially extends primitive identification, while retaining the core clustering, vector extraction, and steering procedures.

E1.justification: TSP, 3-SAT, AIME, GraphNav, and the auxiliary graph-operation tasks are retained. New controls and sensitivity experiments reuse this coverage. The six AIE calibration tasks are newly specified in Appendix B.6, without establishing a change in the tasks previously used.

E2.justification: Appendices F.1 and F.3 add two substantive comparators absent from v1: injection immediately before unembedding as a bag-of-tokens control, and vectors reconstructed from their top-100 decoded tokens. These directly compare alternative explanations with the original primitive vectors; existing unsteered, few-shot, zero-shot, and shuffled-context comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include final-stream injection controls, per-primitive fixed-setting interference evaluation, annotation prompt comparisons, and sweeps over clustering layers, cluster counts, and response counts. Extraction is now reported using 200 responses, versus v1's stated 100. The missing-distance-computation score changes from 500 to 512. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices C.2, F.1–F.3, and G add tests of annotation robustness, lexical explanations of steering, interference between primitives, and sensitivity to clustering hyperparameters and sample size. These substantially extend validation beyond v1's existing injection-layer/magnitude experiments and nearest-neighbor strategy analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies seed counts or repeated-run uncertainty procedures, and existing variability displays are retained. v2 adds correlation and clustering-agreement scores as robustness metrics, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 is numerically unchanged as v2 Table 2. Substantial new results appear in the annotation, control, interference, and robustness analyses. For example, Appendix F.3 reports +2458.5% comparison mentions for the reconstructed vector versus +1103.7% for the original, an acknowledged exception. Appendix G reports correlation above 0.98 between K=50 and K=100 dissimilarity matrices. These are added results, not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a formal expressivity definition and complexity analysis, and corrects the normalization of the mean g from 1/n to 1/m in Section 4.2. Core steering and transfer mathematics remain. The new expressivity definition is internally inconsistent: Equation (5) uses radius divided by unique-token count, whereas the prose specifies the reciprocal.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now explicitly claim an automated LLM annotation capability. The main claims concerning compositional primitive geometry, cross-task transfer, and reasoning finetuning, along with the five-item contribution list, otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends mechanistic interpretation: Appendix F argues against simple token boosting, links interference to sequential algorithmic motifs, and qualifies the reconstruction argument with the comparison-vector exception. Appendices A.7 and G add interpretations connecting expressivity and layer choice to meaningful primitives. The main Discussion's task-coverage and linear-composition limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents AIE calibration tasks, attention-head projection and averaging, and normalization choices in Appendix B.6; GPT-4o prompts and token-context sampling in Appendix C; and hardware and timing in B.7. It reports 5–10 minutes on four A40 GPUs for activation collection and 61 seconds for an example clustering run. The HTML inspection tool is promised for a project website, without establishing release.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hawasly et al., Petukhova et al., and Kopf et al. to motivate latent-space clustering, Han et al. for elbow selection, and Gallegos et al. for the Impact Statement. The broader positioning relative to interpretability and function-vector research remains stable.

P1.justification: The main six-section narrative remains, with localized tightening of methods/results prose, terminology standardization, and repaired appendix references. Existing appendices are reordered, an Impact Statement is added, and the short LLM Usage Disclosure is removed. Much of the increased length documents new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains an annotation stage; existing main figures are rearranged and receive clearer axes and labels. v2 adds a definitions table, extensive annotation and control tables, and robustness Figures 11–13. Retained appendix figures are relocated and resized. One new presentation defect remains: Figure 11's caption describes a panel c that is not displayed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central mechanistic evidence by testing lexical alternatives, examining interference under fixed settings, and checking clustering robustness—important gaps in v1's validation. Detailed extraction and annotation instructions also improve reproducibility, while the reconstruction exception appropriately qualifies the interpretation. The contradictory expressivity formula and missing Figure 11 panel weaken particular additions, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in testing and documenting the core framework.
